newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-IRISH BOSS MCCARTHY PRAISES ICELAND DEFENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRISH BOSS MCCARTHY PRAISES ICELAND DEFENCE.

text.p: Ireland manager Mick McCarthy paid tribute to the Iceland defence that held his side to a 0-0 draw in their World Cup European group eight qualifier at Lansdowne Road on Sunday.
"I think first and foremost, the draw was down to their good defence," said McCarthy.
"I guess if we went away from home and played as well as they did then we would have got something like they did," he added.
Frustrated by the close marking and tough tackling of the Icelanders, who used a five-man defence, Ireland largely relied on set-pieces for scoring opportunities.
It was only when Manchester United's Roy Keane moved into midfield from centre-back following a double substitution in the 64th minute that Ireland showed any creativity.
"I don't think it would have made a great deal of difference if he (Keane) had started in midfield," McCarthy said.
"It was a dull game. These fellows did well to keep it that way."

The nearest Ireland came to scoring was when striker Tony Cascarino rose at the far post in the 21st minute to head back across the goal and inches wide of the post following a corner from midfielder Andy Townsend on the right.
Iceland's best chance fell to striker Helgi Sigurdsson, who was put through on goal by midfielder Heimir Gudjonsson in the 63rd minute but his shot was well saved by goalkeeper Alan Kelly.
The result left Ireland second behind Macedonia on goal difference in the group. Iceland have only Liechtenstein below them.

Ireland: 1-Alan Kelly, 5-Gary Breen, 6-Roy Keane, 4-Phil Babb; 2-Jeff Kenna (13-Kenny Cunningham, 64th), 10-Jason McAteer, 8-Alan McLoughlin, 7-Andy Townsend, 3-Denis Irwin (12-Ian Harte, 64th), 9-David Kelly (15-Alan Moore, 80th), 11-Tony Cascarino.

Iceland: 1-Birkir Kristinsson, 3-Hlynur Birgisson, 5-Olafur Adolfsson, 4-Sigudur Jonsson, 2-Larus Sigurdsson, 7-Agust Gylfason, 8-Heimir Gudjonsson, 6-Runar Kristinsson (14-Arnar Gretarsson, 71), 11-Eyjolfur Sverrisson, 9-Helgi Sigurdsson, 10-Thordur Gudjonsson.
